headlines: With 15 days until the midterms, early voting is underway in at least 30 states, including Texas, and more than 9 million ballots have been cast nationwide.
President Trump campaigns in ruby-red Kansas as part of a seven-day, seven-state blitz, stumping for Senator Roger Marshall in his tight race against Democratic pastor Adam Hamilton.
A new ABC News/Washington Post/Ipsos poll puts President Trump's approval rating at a record-low 33%, with 72% of voters saying the country is heading in the wrong direction.
A 24-year-old Kansas man was arrested after allegedly posting public threats to kill President Trump at his rally in Wichita.
In Michigan's closely watched open Senate race, nearly 10% of registered voters have already cast ballots as Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers remain in a virtual toss-up.
Michigan Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers defended leaked audio about using off-duty police officers as Detroit poll watchers, saying he wants voting to be 'easy to vote, hard to cheat.'
Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed said Israel is not a U.S. ally, accusing it of genocide and apartheid and criticizing American foreign policy.

Curfews are in place across multiple French cities after violent anti-government protests and riots left a nearly 150-year-old town hall in Limoges engulfed in flames and more than 3,000 businesses ransacked or vandalized.
The NFL says Sunday's game in Paris between the Steelers and Saints will go on despite the unrest in France.
At least four Canadian soldiers were killed and dozens injured in a deadly fire at a military base in Alberta that began with an explosion during a live-fire training exercise.
President Zelenskyy says President Trump is pushing Ukraine to surrender to Russia as U.S. support weakens, and ABC's team in Ukraine was forced into bunkers multiple times by Russian attacks.
Trump said Zelenskyy 'doesn't know what he's talking about' and suggested it may be time for Ukraine to find someone else to negotiate, while not ruling out meeting with Putin and Xi Jinping.
A Roman Catholic priest, Father Patricio Alfredo Sanchez Molinari, was killed during a live-streamed Mass in Ecuador when a wooden crucifix fell from the wall and struck his head.

Two more Charlotte-Mecklenburg police officers resigned after allegedly sharing racist text messages discovered during an investigation into misuse of Flock cameras, bringing the total to seven officers named.

Newly unsealed court documents in the O.J. Simpson murder case raise questions about a possible accomplice and the still-missing murder weapon, with a now-deceased informant allegedly providing information about its disposal.
A new nor'easter is threatening the East Coast with wind gusts topping 50 mph, rough surf and waves up to 15 feet, prompting coastal flood alerts from New Jersey to the Outer Banks.
Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the season after blood clots were found in his lungs, following an earlier diagnosis of a superficial clot in his calf.

The USDA announced the recall of more than 1.5 million pounds of ready-to-eat meat and poultry distributed by K-M Foods, including sausage, hot dogs, bacon and deli meat, over a warehouse cooling system malfunction.

Mississippi's attorney general said a deputy was justified in the fatal shooting of one-year-old Cohen Wiley during a shoplifting investigation at a Walmart, a account disputed by the boy's mother and family attorney.

The 34-year-old woman who drove her pickup truck onto a children's soccer field in Wichita, Kansas, killing two people including a 6-year-old and injuring ten others, has been released without charges pending toxicology and mechanical exams.
Federal investigators say a San Diego ticket broker used 1,300 accounts to buy thousands of tickets to a single Beyoncé concert in Kansas City and made more than $800,000 in resale profits.
Selena Gomez said vaping nicotine 'changed my voice' and encouraged followers to quit after being criticized for changes in her appearance and voice.
Dancing with the Stars pro Val Chmerkovskiy was suspended for one week after referencing Will Smith's Oscar slap in a social media post following a harsh critique from judge Carrie Ann Inaba.
A Pennsylvania teenager who won homecoming king immediately gave his crown and sash to the runner-up, a fellow student with Down syndrome, who was moved to tears.

Grammy-winning artist Lil Jon discussed his new memoir 'I Only Shout So You Can Hear Me,' covering his Georgia roots, learning his biological father's identity, the death of his son Nathan, and his turn to meditation and health.
President Trump is ramping up campaign efforts for GOP candidates with just over two weeks until the midterm elections, starting with a rally in Kansas today.
New NBC News polling shows 71% of Americans believe the U.S. is on the wrong track, with the economy and soaring gas prices from the war with Iran as top voter concerns.
President Trump's approval rating has dropped to 34% as he rallies for Republicans in red states like Kentucky, telling voters to act like he is on the ballot.

Republican incumbent Senator Roger Marshall faces a surprisingly tight race in Kansas against Democratic megachurch pastor Adam Hamilton, who raised significantly more money in the three months leading up to October.

Hundreds of "No Kings Day" rallies organized by a network of the same name were held across the U.S. from California to Florida, with protesters condemning President Trump and demanding he keep his hands off the vote.
The NBC News Decision Desk poll shows Democrats with a nine-point advantage on the generic ballot, though Republicans hold an edge among less-motivated voters.
The NBC News poll finds 44% of Americans say their personal financial situation is worse than a year ago, up from 34% in September 2025, with a majority of independents saying they are worse off.
Two-thirds of voters say gas prices have been a serious problem for their families, and 34% call it a very serious problem, up from 29% in the spring.
The NBC News poll shows Democrats with a 12-point edge among all adults on which party they trust more to handle inflation and the rising cost of everyday things.
Voters hold unfavorable views of both parties, with 63% viewing Republicans unfavorably and 57% viewing Democrats unfavorably, according to the NBC News poll.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Meet the Press that the Trump administration will "own the economy," citing a million private sector jobs and record household net worth, and called rising prices an energy supply-side shock.

President Trump told NBC's Peter Nicholas that White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles will be there "until the end" and has done a great job, denying he is unhappy with her after former press secretary Katie Zachariah left after just five days.
Ukraine launched more than 1,000 drones at Russia in one of the largest aerial attacks of the war, hitting an oil depot in Saint Petersburg and setting it on fire.
President Trump paused implementation of further sanctions against Russia that won bipartisan approval in Congress, amid deepening divisions with Ukraine.

In an exclusive Meet the Press interview, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine would find it "very difficult" to win without U.S. support and called it a historic mistake and big tragedy if the U.S. sided with Russia.

A developing nor'easter off the Carolina coast is expected to bring wind gusts up to 50 mph, coastal flooding of 2 to 4 feet, beach erosion, and 8 to 14 foot waves along the Eastern Seaboard from North Carolina to the Jersey Shore.
Tropical Storm Trudy, which impacted parts of Mexico over the weekend, continues to weaken with 60 mph winds as it heads west.

31 million people are under frost and freeze advisories as a cold October chill brings temperatures in the 30s, with rain and possible flash flooding expected in parts of California and the Southwest.

Two people, including a six-year-old boy, were killed and nearly a dozen others ranging from 5 to 68 years old were injured after a woman drove her truck through a youth soccer game at a Wichita, Kansas sports complex.
Authorities identified the two people killed in the Wichita soccer game crash as 35-year-old Nicholas Schaefer and six-year-old Cole Adrian.

A 34-year-old woman was taken into custody and released without charges pending toxicology results and a mechanical examination of the truck after the Wichita crash; her two children were in the vehicle at the time.

Students in Bend, Oregon will not attend classes today as the community mourns those killed in last week's shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School, where a 16-year-old opened fire, killing a teacher and three children including a five-year-old.
The victims of the Silver Rail Elementary shooting include five-year-old Rome Summer and 25-year-old teacher Megan Lambert, while a seven-year-old and 54-year-old teacher Becky Drury were injured.
Law enforcement sources tell NBC News the 16-year-old Silver Rail Elementary gunman obtained the gun from his mother, who purchased it in August and is cooperating with the investigation.
Investigators are searching the Bend shooting suspect's devices and home, where another 44 rounds of ammunition were found, to determine a motive.
France is on edge after a weekend of major unrest, with largely peaceful protests over the cost of living and the state of education spiraling into rioting and looting and thousands arrested.
Authorities say about half a million people took to the streets in France on Saturday, with 2,500 arrests made and around 1,000 police officers and fire personnel injured in clashes with rioters.
Rioters in Limoges burned a 19th-century city hall that had survived two world wars to the ground, and the Louvre Museum in Paris was unable to open due to student protesters at its main entrances.

The French prime minister announced curfews in some parts of France as President Emmanuel Macron addressed the nation, saying he understood the pain of rising prices but that there is no justification for violence.
France's interior minister offered his resignation to President Macron, but it was not accepted and he was told to go back and organize a response.
